P009.finding: A 40 × 28 mm CS-LITE baffle aperture reduces the modeled bright area outside the image from 80.98% to 23.93% of open area, with 1.25 mm minimum field clearance.
P009.method: CineStill publishes a 6.5 × 4.4 in housing and 5⅞ × 3¾ in illuminated field, converted to millimeters in the drawing. For the first mask, take the projected 35.8 × 23.8 mm frame out of the total aperture area. For the revision, account for lateral registration error of 0.5 mm and additional geometric inset from a 10° ray through 2 mm stock. The P008 carrier controls negative registration. This P009 bundle coupon tests the separate interface between that kind of carrier and the named light.
P009.physical: Measure where the lit area actually sits in the housing. Use uncropped RAW flat-field captures to check edge-to-center exposure, color variation, shadowing and stray light for each operating mode.
P009.source: The CS-LITE's lit field and exterior size come from CineStill. Centering between each rectangular component, film field dimensions and ray angles are modeled. The bright-area ratio is geometric. Actual uniformity, glare and spectrum require measurement. [CineStill CS-LITE specifications](https://cinestillfilm.com/collections/135/products/cs-litecamera-scanning-light-source-1?variant=42245876646060)
P009.use: Cut the opaque mask with the center aperture. The blue rectangles mark the published host envelope and lit region. Measure the actual window to register the mask accurately before closing the stack.

P011.finding: Tightening the Disc index shoe reduces modeled angular freedom from 1.65° to 0.43° and leaves 0.17 mm worst indexed frame margin.
P011.method: A fifteen-position ring places a 10.6 × 8.2 mm rectangular target tangentially at 24 mm radius. Replay all index gaps and sweep the angular free play of a 2 mm pin in the exported slot, spanning ±0.43° in the revision. Then charge 0.25 mm lateral spindle and seating allowance against the smallest aperture margin. Disc OD of 65 mm, hub, frame radius, scanner footprint and key engagement are adjustable synthetic coupon inputs.
P011.physical: Measure the actual disc hub, film plane, detent or original die-cut notch geometry and frame radii on sacrificial film. Verify the follower engages the hub with clear access, does not contact sensitized image areas and leaves the actual V600 calibration path clear.
P011.source: Disc media has a ring of fifteen small 8 × 10 mm class images. The drawing uses the 10.6 × 8.2 mm example documented by Lippisches Kamera Museum. Epson documents V600 transparency placement and holder detection. [Kodak Disc exhibit](https://www.lippisches-kameramuseum.de/Zubehoer_Foto/Film_Kodak_Disc.htm) · [Film Photography Project format summary](https://filmphotographyproject.com/shooting-sub-miniature-film/) · [Epson V600 user guide](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/prv6ph/prv6phug.pdf)
P011.use: The carrier, spindle bore, single exposure opening and index shoe are cut patterns. The engraved ring is a manual index ruler. The blue disc boundary, projected image and pin footprint guide measurement of the real film.

P012.finding: Adding intermediate edge clips lowers the modeled free-edge rise from 3.82 to 0.44 mm while preserving 0.50 mm clamp-to-image clearance.
P012.method: For a 46 mm-wide 127 specimen with a single 40 × 40 mm image, model the curled edge between stations as a circular arc with 130 mm minimum radius. Add ±0.30 mm placement at both stations, then compute sagitta over the worst free span. The single-image coupon uses another V600 envelope and shares the marker-preservation workflow. It tests longitudinal curl at the two edges. The open center and cross-film bow still need observation.
P012.physical: Measure a representative range of aged 127 strip curvatures, including roller-set and cross-film curl. Verify clip retention and contact marks outside the frame, then check sharpness and Epson transparency calibration.
P012.source: The Film Photography Project supplies 46 mm 127 film information. Dimensions for 40 mm square exposure, curl radius, clip error and the V600 placement coupon are trial inputs. [Film Photography Project 127 format](https://filmphotographyproject.com/film-photography-podcast-365-127-format-film/) · [Epson V600 user guide](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/prv6ph/prv6phug.pdf)
P012.use: Cut the carrier, mask opening and separate edge strips. Use the four scored stations per edge for prototype retainer positions and gauge the clip tip before contact with film.

P013.finding: Using a single asymmetric key gives 0.20 mm seating margin for the forward specimen and rejects the reflected single-perforation position.
P013.method: The modeled 35 mm-wide coupon has a 28 mm square exposure and one 2.8 × 1.8 mm perforation at x = −4.00 mm and y = −15.75 mm from its image center. Apply 0.15 mm location error to each key edge. Check all forward key engagements and try the reflected hole across the strip centerline to catch any misleading partial engagement. The older two-sided assumption binds in the forward direction and provides a misleading cue at one pin when reflected.
P013.physical: Measure the actual 126 strip’s perforation and its frame offset. Use a soft retractable pin, verify registration without forcing or stretching the perforation, and inspect edge crops and host calibration.
P013.source: Science Museum Group records 26 mm and 28 mm square 126 camera frames across models. The trial targets the 28 mm case. Individual perforation size, offset, and reflective orientation are modeled. [Science Museum Group cartridge camera collection](https://collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk/search/object_type/cartridge-camera) · [Film Photography Project 126 format](https://filmphotographyproject.com/126-instamatic-film-history-status/) · [Epson V600 user guide](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/prv6ph/prv6phug.pdf)
P013.use: Cut the carrier and key stock. Use the marked pin and perforation centers as layout references. Read the datum from the emulsion orientation observed on the actual machine.

P014.finding: The three-height shim coupon spans 0.50 mm and offers 0.17 mm worst-case reserve within a hypothetical focus band.
P014.method: Test three physical shim section heights 0.95, 1.20 and 1.45 mm against a 0.90–1.50 mm trial focus band. Charge ±0.13 mm combined seating and thickness error. Search the available shims for the best minimum reserve across both boundaries. The selector enables a real focus sweep before locking down a carrier dimension. A 56 × 56 mm square exposure checks a single 6×6 case in 61 mm nominal stock.
P014.physical: Measure glass-to-emulsion offsets with the real V600, fit the shims without blocking factory holder markers, and compare center and corner target sharpness at every height and both curl orientations.
P014.source: Epson documents medium-format film loading and holder recognition details for the V600. Ilford documents 120 medium-format stock. The SVG footprint, film width, square frame and height range are adjustable coupon assumptions. [Epson V600 user guide](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/prv6ph/prv6phug.pdf) · [Ilford 120 medium-format film](https://www.ilfordphoto.com/delta-100-professional-120?___from_store=ilford_uk&___store=ilford_brochure)
P014.use: The three full-size thickness silhouettes identify candidate shim heights. Cut the carrier aperture and position two equal-height shims at the scored feet. Measure installed height before optical tests.

P015.finding: Four windows on 19 mm pitch leave 0.375 mm worst crop registration margin and 0.85 mm of opaque land between crops.
P015.method: Match four adjacent model frames (17.0 × 12.8 mm) across a 16 mm wide strip with +/−0.20 mm load and alignment allowance total. The outer bays of the 18.15 mm baseline pitch clip image edges and leave no opaque land. The 19 mm spacing meets the all-frame envelope and minimizes the opaque separator's land requirement. This trial uses an Epson 4870 candidate, whose guide explicitly reserves top-of-platen calibration space, with a different placeholder keepout height from the V600 coupons.
P015.physical: Confirm the 4870 transparency unit and software with a manual marquee, then measure the top clear calibration zone, actual film pitch, both edge support lines and the minimum focus stand-off. Check retained frames for scratches and corner falloff.
P015.source: Film Photography Project documents 16 mm 110 stock and approximately 13 × 17 mm nominal frames. Epson 4870 documentation requires keeping its calibration space uncovered. The numeric hold-down and clearance regions, actual exposed crop target and pitch are adjustable estimates. [110 stock width](https://filmphotographyproject.com/110-film-photography/) · [110 nominal frame](https://filmphotographyproject.com/shooting-sub-miniature-film/) · [Epson 4870 quick reference](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/pr48ph/pr48phqr.pdf)
P015.use: Cut four windows and two rails. Center the frame strip by its images in the manual preview. Unblocked calibration and edge overlap require physical fit checks.

P016.finding: An offset 3.67 × 5.22 mm still window preserves 0.059 mm minimum image margin through the modeled pose sweep and excludes the neighboring images and perforation side.
P016.method: Use a 3.30 × 4.60 mm Standard 8 reading area, 3.81 mm pitch, ±1° yaw and ±0.07 mm placement in the modeled film infeed. Evaluate target corners, neighboring frame margins and the perforation-side keepout independently. A mirror-centered window clips the useful area and admits the perforated side. Offset the opening by 0.96 mm toward the image side. The modeled margin is small enough to require physical registration verification.
P016.physical: Verify Standard 8 on examples of the actual archived stock, perforation side and picture orientation. Check print scale and use a measurable alignment ruler to test real still-frame inspection. Inspect abrasions and compare optical resolution with a camera-copy setup.
P016.source: Australia’s National Film and Sound Archive documents Standard 8 and Super 8’s different perforations. Film Photography Project makes perforated Standard 8 stock. The mount uses trial-specific frame size, pitch, pitch-axis registration, perforation zone and manual V600 orientation. [NFSA audiovisual format register](https://www.nfsa.gov.au/sites/default/files/07-2017/avregistryweb.pdf) · [Standard 8 stock](https://filmphotographyproject.com/introducing-fpp-cine8-regular-8mm-film/) · [Epson V600 user guide](https://files.support.epson.com/pdf/prv6ph/prv6phug.pdf)
P016.use: Use the small opening and the two pressure strips to prototype a single-image inspection coupon. The neighboring frames and blue perforation band are inspection references.
